file.content: Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation results vary across reproductions, but variance sources interact, and their relative importance shifts with the benchmark format. We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory) in a fully crossed design with up to seven facets across eight open-weight instruction-tuned models (7--9B parameters) and five benchmarks, totaling approximately 2.3 million evaluation records. D-study projections show that a recommended multi-condition design achieves $G \geq 0.80$ with 178 items (1,602 evaluations per model), a 3.1$\times$ item reduction over single-condition designs (552 items, 552 evaluations)---trading approximately 3$\times$ more evaluations per item for 3$\times$ fewer items, a tradeoff that favors multi-condition designs when item construction is costly. Model$\times$item interaction (up to 36\%) indicates that models differ primarily in which items they find difficult, not in overall ability. Preliminary validation across a 3B--72B parameter range confirms stable variance structure within one architecture family. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator for evaluation design optimization.

**结论：推荐保持当前标题不变（Option C）。**

当前标题："Reproducibility Budgets for Open-Weight LLM Evaluation: A Generalizability Theory Study of 7--9B Instruction-Tuned Models"

如果 Director 倾向显式标注，可考虑在副标题改为 "A Generalizability Theory Study under Binary Scoring"，但我认为当前已充分。

**结论：[severity: warning] Probit 连续方差分量的原始输出未找到。**

**建议**：明确 MF3 的交付物要求——如果是"展示连续 vs binary 的方差分量对比表"，需要 Agent 重跑；如果是"加强现有 probit 段落的说服力"，当前素材够用。

**结论：Director 的 "G_model < 0.3" 仅在单 item 单条件下成立，需要更精确的表述。**

主要误差：σ²_{M×p}/n_p（model×item 30.2% 除以 item 数）
